correctness.rationale: For split-product parameters r=ph and s=qh in lowest terms, p=2 is equivalent to r=2s, so the X^(1/2) integral-point contribution occupies only O(L) parameter pairs. Summing this locus and treating p>=3 separately gives the raw exponent 1/2+5 theta. Substitution into the inspected witness-forest bounds yields 1/2+7 theta for short rejected length. Li's explicit 1/24 short-prime theorem then gives 17/24+epsilon and 19/24+epsilon, with long-gap mass controlled by its logarithmically small exceptional set.

originality.rationale: The inspected Chojecki preprint states 4/5 and 9/10 and does not isolate the r=2s degree-two locus or state the transfer exponents. Searches for 17/24, 19/24, the sparse degree-two refinement, and equivalent quantitative-deficiency formulations did not identify prior coverage. A related Ryan Kielhorn Zenodo preprint was identified but its full text was not inspected, so it remains an explicit residual originality risk.

value.rationale: The result sharpens the quantitative bottleneck in a recent density-one construction, reducing the short rejected-length exponent from 9/10 to 19/24+epsilon and the raw short-gap exponent to 17/24+epsilon, while also extracting a reusable transfer rule from almost-all short-prime exponents to construction deficiency exponents.
